feature_story.headline: 1978 in Motion: Dance Floors, Marquees, and Living Rooms
feature_story.deck: A short field report on how music, movies, and television are shaping one shared year.
paragraphs: 1978 feels like a hinge year, where radio hits such as Night Fever carry club energy into everyday streets, cabs, and corner stores.
Artists including Bee Gees and Donna Summer are proving that polished production can still feel immediate, social, and physical.
At the multiplex, Grease and Superman confirm that theatrical scale matters, even as Mork and Mindy keeps families tied to weekly television habits.
The result is a culture that moves on multiple tracks at once: dance floor urgency, screen-sized spectacle, and living-room ritual.
sidebar_facts: Radio momentum: Night Fever, Hot Stuff, Le Freak
Box office pressure: Grease, Superman, Animal House
TV watch-list: Mork and Mindy, WKRP in Cincinnati
feature_story.quote: 1978 is less a conclusion than a high-speed midpoint.
